title: Why arrays start at zero (not one)
description:
Byte asks Compy why the first item in a list is number zero. The answer is about distance, not tradition.

#coding #python #programming #shorts
angle: An index is not a position, it is a distance from the start, so the first item is zero steps away.
hook: Ever wondered why arrays start counting at zero?

scenes.speaker: byte
scenes.narration: Ever wondered why arrays start counting at zero?

scenes.speaker: compy
scenes.narration: Stick around. It's not tradition. It's the computer being lazy, in a very smart way.

scenes.speaker: byte
scenes.narration: Okay. Three snacks: pizza, tacos, fries. Give me snack number one.

scenes.speaker: byte
scenes.narration: That's tacos. I asked for the first snack. I'm now emotionally invested in the pizza.

scenes.speaker: compy
scenes.narration: You asked for a position. I only track distance. Pizza is zero steps from the start.

scenes.speaker: compy
scenes.narration: Think of memory as a street. Pizza's at the start. Tacos are one house down. Fries, two.

scenes.speaker: byte
scenes.narration: Huh. So the index isn't which one. It's how far. That's... actually kind of obvious now.

scenes.speaker: compy
scenes.narration: If we started at one, I'd subtract one on every lookup. Billions of times a day. For no reason.

props.code:
# starting at 1 would cost
addr = start + (i - 1)

# starting at 0 is free
addr = start + i

scenes.speaker: byte
scenes.narration: So if I ask for snack three, the street just ends. Error. Fair.

scenes.speaker: compy
scenes.narration: Rule of the day: the last index is length minus one. Or just use negative one. Less to think about.

scenes.speaker: byte
scenes.narration: That's it. Follow for more. Next up: recursion, a function that calls itself.

props.next: Recursion, a function that calls itself

claims.text: Zero-based numbering is common in programming because an index is an offset from the first element
Dijkstra argued for zero-based numbering in his 1982 note 'Why numbering should start at zero'
